_fixture.reference: NCT02130024 (RIVAL, ranibizumab vs aflibercept, treat-and-extend). The protocol PDF is not in the repository; only the public registry summary was available.
from_registry: Three monthly loading injections at Baseline, Week 4 and Week 8.
From Week 8 the interval follows disease activity: no activity extends the interval by 2 weeks up to 12 weeks; activity shortens it as the protocol specifies.
Assessments read by a Central Reading Center at Month 12 and Month 24 (baseline anchored).
assumptions: A1 One activity sign after an extension shortens the interval by 2 weeks; two or more signs return it to 4 weeks (the task's synthetic rule; the registry only says 'reduced as specified').

A2 Fourth-extension breakpoint: once three extensions have been attempted, an extension is capped at the longest interval that ended with activity minus 2 weeks; the cap is recorded when first reached.
A3 Intervals are bounded to 4-12 weeks; the next target counts from the previous injection's actual date.
A4 Injection window +/-7 days; Month 12 = Day 364 and Month 24 = Day 728 from baseline, each +/-14 days.
A5 An injection due inside the Month 12 or Month 24 window is given at that assessment visit on the injection's own date (one visit, both sets of assessments).

A6 The reading centre recommends an interval in weeks; the calculated interval books the visit and a differing recommendation is shown (precedence 'calculated'). Scenario A8 also runs 'review' and 'shorter'.
A7 The finding is confirmed by the investigator (role pi); the recommendation may be recorded by pi or crc.

protocol.title: Synthetic treat-and-extend schedule modelled on NCT02130024

steps.label: Two or more signs: back to 4 weeks

adaptive.source: Synthetic fixture, assumptions A1-A3 and A6
adaptive.quote: If none of the signs were present, the subsequent injection interval was extended by 2-week increments up until a maximum of 12-weekly intervals was reached.
